decisions.executionNote: Approach the two front upright supports with open grippers, gradually pitching down while preserving elbow-up continuity; object positions estimated from RGB.
Align jaws with the front blocks' visible yaw and descend toward their sides. Keep open until wrist views confirm centering.
Recentering the blocks in each wrist view, closing fully, then lifting 2 cm to verify retention visually.
Both blocks remain between the jaws after the test lift. Raise for clearance and carry to symmetric lower-support locations, correcting yaw upright.
Lower and release the first two supports symmetrically, slightly forward of the unused blocks to avoid contact. Check their upright stance after release.
Withdraw above the released supports, then spread to approach the long board from its two ends while turning the open jaws.
Finish opposing end-grasp orientation and descend outside the support footprints, using wider end positions to avoid the upright blocks.
Use wrist views to center the long board between both jaws, descend to its edges, and close both grippers before a test lift.
Large residuals suggest edge contact rather than a secure grasp. Open and lift clear, then align farther over the board ends for a vertical descent.
Align with the board's shifted center and grasp farther toward its ends to clear the nearby supports; descend slowly with jaws open.
The wrist views show the jaws offset toward the supports. Lift slightly, recenter away from them, and descend with the board centered in the open jaws.
Close on the centered board and make a small bilateral test lift. Watch board retention and whether nearby supports settle upright after jaws withdraw.
Board rises with both jaws. Level its ends, lift clear of the supports, and translate over the support pair while keeping both grippers closed.
Lower the board over the support pair and release near contact so it can settle flat; its pitch is uncertain in the head view. Withdraw vertically for inspection.
The released board appears edge-up rather than flat. Regrasp, lift clear, and gently roll both wrists together about the board center to correct its pitch.
The board did not follow the previous lift, so the grasp was empty. Open and descend to its actual upper edge with tilted jaws, then close and verify with a short lift.
Lift the newly grasped board clear and apply a small coordinated positive pitch correction about its center. Inspect the broad face before attempting placement.
The narrow board face still suggests a steep pitch. Continue a controlled bilateral roll while compensating the wrist arc to keep the board clear of the blocks.
The broad board face is now visible and nearly level. Apply a small final pitch correction and lower toward the upright support pair without releasing yet.
The board is level and centered over the supports. Descend slowly another 3 cm, keeping both jaws closed and monitoring clearance.
Set the level board onto the support tops, open both grippers, and withdraw outward and backward to inspect the lower layer without disturbing it.
The lower board remains on its supports after release. Lift away and unwind the board-handling wrist roll before approaching the remaining upright blocks.
Previous motion was rejected before execution. Retry the wrist unwind and lift at one-quarter increments to preserve joint continuity near the current configuration.
Continue lifting and unwinding in small increments. The board shifted after release, so inspect its support alignment once the grippers are clear before adding layers.
Approach the shifted board ends from above with open opposing jaws. The left end appears lower, so plan an asymmetric regrasp to level and recenter it on both supports.
Center each jaw pair on its local board end using wrist views, descend farther at the low left end, and regrasp without changing the board pitch.
Lift and move the board away from the nearby blocks before further leveling; the open jaws appear to have contacted the supports during the regrasp.
With the board clear, correct its steep pitch and yaw together while keeping both grips closed and compensating the wrist arc.
Continue rolling the securely held board toward horizontal with a slight lift of its center; keep the end heights matched and inspect before lowering.
The board now appears level. Move its center forward over the actual support tops and lower partway, retaining both grips until contact is visually checked.
Descend vertically in small matched increments with the board centered over the supports. Keep both grips closed until the remaining height gap is checked.
Release the board near support contact, then retreat backward before lifting to avoid hooking its edges. Inspect stability and centering after the jaws clear.
Clear the released board and unwind the wrists. The board appears offset toward the front of the support tops; obtain an unobstructed view before recentering or adding the next layer.
The previous unwind was rejected with zero motion. Retry from the unchanged observation with much smaller rotations and lift increments to preserve IK continuity.
Lift and finish unwinding clear of the board. It moved during withdrawal, so the next placement will retract strictly outward from the ends rather than dragging backward.
Switch to a more vertical top-down grasp over the board to avoid wedging its edges upward. Approach at clearance with both jaws open.
Descend straight down with jaws straddling the board width; keep the vertical orientation unchanged to prevent the earlier edge-up rotation.
The left open jaw appears to contact the nearby support. Shift it slightly backward, restore vertical alignment, then close both jaws and test a straight lift.
The vertical grasp retains the board flat. Lift clear, carry it over the support pair, and gently correct the small yaw and end-height differences.
Lower the flat board vertically toward both support tops while preserving the secure top-down grasp and its current centering.
Settle the board the final few millimeters onto the supports, open both jaws, and withdraw strictly vertically to avoid dragging the layer.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Move above the rear blocks with open jaws while the completed lower board remains undisturbed.
Align each vertical gripper to its rear block's visible yaw and descend toward the block sides, keeping clear of the lower board.
Lift clear before correcting the left block's yaw alignment. Shift the right approach slightly rearward to avoid contacting the lower board with an open finger.
Descend to the upper sides of the aligned rear blocks, close fully, and test retention with a short vertical lift before carrying them onto the lower board.
Both rear blocks appear retained. Lift above the lower board, correct their yaw, and carry them to symmetric middle-support positions with both grippers closed.
The lower board shifted during block pickup. Move the held blocks to clear rear-side staging positions so the lower layer can be repaired without nearby finger collisions.
Set the two retained blocks upright at clear rear-side staging locations, accounting for their slightly different grasp heights, and release before repairing the board.
Withdraw from the staged blocks and approach above the tipped board. The rear blocks are now clear, allowing repair without the earlier nearby collisions.
Use closed fingertips outside the support footprints to gently tip the board forward onto a flat face, avoiding a difficult edge grasp and keeping the supports untouched.
The board slid rather than tipping. Raise the closed fingertips to contact its upper edge, then apply a small synchronized forward push to lay it flat.
The board has fallen flat. Align vertical jaws near its outer ends, outside the support footprints, and descend for a flat bilateral grasp.
Close both vertical grippers on the flat board and lift straight up, preserving its pitch and checking retention before translating over the supports.
Carry the flat board to the actual support-top centers, which are farther back than the earlier target, correcting its small yaw while remaining above contact.
Lower the final 24 mm onto the aligned supports, open both jaws, and lift straight up without horizontal dragging.
The left end settled lower after release. Regrasp and lift the board to expose the lower supports for inspection rather than adding an unstable layer.
The previous grasp was empty. Recenter over the actual sloping board using the head and wrist views and descend to its lower left and higher right edges.
Lift clear of the support-adjacent grasp sites. Switch to a left-side center grasp of the board, with the right arm withdrawn, to avoid repeatedly contacting the supports.
Replan after the rejected right-arm step: hold that arm stationary. Pinch the board's upper edge near its center with the left jaw, clear of both supports, and test retention.
The center pinch retained the board. Lift it clear and forward, then begin rolling its upper edge toward a flat orientation; retract the idle right arm from its extended posture.
Continue rolling the retained board toward a flat face while lowering the wrist to keep it clear at a manageable height. Hold the right arm still; the board's unsupported end remains uncertain.
Tracking worsened near the left arm's configuration limit. Retract the held board toward the robot without further rotation to regain joint margin and keep the right arm stationary.
The single pinch allows the unsupported board end to droop. Lower it into the clear foreground, release it to settle flat, and withdraw before returning to a stable two-handed vertical grasp.
Approach the now-flat long board at two separated points, matching its diagonal yaw with vertical jaws. Keep clearance above the board before the final descent.
Refine the two grasp centers from wrist views, correcting the left wrist's small tilt and moving the right jaws toward the board before closing.
Close the two vertical grasps and lift the long board clear of the middle board. Preserve its flat orientation and verify both ends rise together.
Carry the flat retained board above the actual support pair. Match their slight diagonal alignment rather than assuming equal fore-aft positions, and remain above contact.
Lower the board vertically 30 mm while preserving its alignment with the staggered support tops. Keep both grips closed until the contact height is checked.
The board barely moved during descent, consistent with resting on the supports. Open both jaws fully and withdraw vertically to check stability without dragging it.
The lower board remains across both supports after withdrawal. Approach the staged rear blocks from above, moving outward and lowering to regain left-arm extension margin.
Center on the staged blocks using the wrist views, match their small yaw angles, descend to their upper sides, and close both grippers away from the lower layer.
Lift the staged blocks above the lower board while moving away from the rear reach limit, then carry inward toward the two middle-support locations. Keep both grippers closed.
Bring the retained blocks inward and align their visible footprints with the diagonal lower board, lowering slowly while preserving elbow-up continuity near the left reach limit.
